steps.title: Local Disk vs Object Store
steps.text: Object stores like S3 and Azure Blob offer virtually unlimited capacity with 11-nines durability and pay-per-use pricing, trading latency (5-50ms) for elastic scalability.

steps.title: Zero-Disk Architecture
steps.text: In zero-disk mode, the Surgewave broker becomes stateless by writing segments directly to object storage. This enables easy horizontal scaling and instant instance replacement.

steps.title: Hybrid Storage Strategies
steps.text: Most production deployments benefit from hybrid: fast local NVMe for recent hot data and cheap object storage for older cold data, with age-based or size-based tiering policies.

steps.title: Alternative Storage Engines
steps.text: Surgewave supports pluggable engines: RocksDB for high write throughput, SQLite for edge deployments, DuckDB for OLAP queries, LMDB for ultra-fast reads, and NVMe-Direct for raw performance.

steps.title: Best Practices
steps.text: Start with local disk and tier later, use managed identity in cloud, set lifecycle policies, monitor egress costs, and always benchmark with your actual workload before committing.
